Yesterday, CMS announced that 524,909 Texas children have been disenrolled from Medicaid and CHIP, which is the highest number in the nation and makes up nearly 24% of all children who have lost Medicaid or CHIP coverage in the US since renewals began in March 2023.

(1/2)

Good news: Today, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services approved increasing postpartum #Medicaid and #CHIP coverage in Texas to 12 months after pregnancy.

An estimated 137k more Texas moms and babies will now be eligible for health care coverage post-pregnancy – a huge win for Texas! #MaternalHealth

14 years ago, the Affordable Care Act was signed into law!

Since then, the #ACA has provided Americans with quality, affordable health coverage.

Let’s continue to build on this process and make health care more affordable and accessible for everyone. https://t.co/MpIGVBJNox

This afternoon, I met with Roberto Haddad with DHR Health in Edinburg.

We discussed improving health care in South Texas by supporting safety-net hospitals, which serve patients regardless of insurance status.

I will continue to fight for affordable, accessible health care in South Texas.

Today, I honored the life of Dr. Paul Raymond Buitrón, MD, for his 49 years of service to patients in Laredo and all of South Texas.

Born and raised in Laredo, he found a passion in the medical field and built strong relationships with all of his patients.

I presented his son with a Congressional Certificate of Recognition to ensure Dr. Buitrón's service to South Texas is memorialized.

Today, I announced $100,000 in grant funding for MedCognition for HAZMAT training. 

MedCognition will use this funding to research more effective training methods for HAZMAT professionals. 

Training will be centered on treating patients who have been exposed to poisonous gas, corrosive materials, and poisonous gas. 

I will continue to fight for medical treatment and advancements for our district and ensure our safety.

Medicare is helping Americans, including families across TX-28, save more than ever on prescription drugs. This program is making a real difference in lowering healthcare costs and ensuring access to vital medications. 

Don’t miss your chance to get the coverage you need—Medicare Open Enrollment is open now through December 7. Visit https://t.co/PIvMkfGj10 to explore your options, compare plans, and secure the best coverage for you and your loved ones.

This afternoon, my Legislative Correspondent, Zachary Johnson, met with representatives from the Texas Organization of Rural and Community Hospitals. They discussed the presence of rural hospitals in the district and policy matters related to healthcare in Texas. I look forward to supporting them and their efforts to provide healthcare for rural Texans.

Today, I visited the Ruthe B. Cowl Rehabilitation Center and had the opportunity to see the incredible work they do to support patients on their road to recovery. RBC focuses on improving mobility, balance, and independence while helping patients recover from illness or injury.  

The center provides essential services, including physical, occupational, and speech therapy, as well as internship opportunities for future healthcare professionals. Their dedication to minimizing risks for patients and clinicians while increasing efficiency is truly commendable. I appreciate the important role they play in our community and look forward to supporting their mission.

Today, my wife, Imelda, attended the ASAS Health Partners Western Theme Patient Appreciation Party! It was a fun and memorable event, bringing everyone together to celebrate and show appreciation for the wonderful patients. https://t.co/FjViZqb2XY

This morning, I met with @NACHC President and CEO @KyuRheeMD, Chief Policy Officer Joe Dunn, Christine Pellerin, and my dear friend, former Congressman Henry Bonilla, to discuss their vital work expanding access to primary care. In #TX28 alone, more than 325,000 patients rely on six federally funded health center organizations operating 23 unique delivery sites – many serving rural communities.

These centers are a lifeline for South Texas. However, under the partisan budget bill – which I voted against – devastating cuts to Medicare and Medicaid threaten care for tens of thousands of people in our district.

I'll keep fighting in Congress to protect health care and the essential programs our communities depend on.

Seniors deserve access to early and comprehensive cancer screenings. That’s why I cosponsored the bipartisan Nancy Gardner Sewell Act to expand Medicare coverage for multi-cancer early detection tests.

This bill creates a clear path for @US_FDA-approved tests that can detect multiple cancers early – saving lives, improving outcomes, and lowering costs.

Cancer touches every family. I’ll keep working across the aisle to make sure seniors in South Texas and across the country have access to lifesaving innovations in cancer detection.

With vital health insurance tax credits under threat, monthly premiums for 113,000 people in #TX28 are set to skyrocket. The program serves everyone from small business owners to rural communities, and allowing it to expire could result in complete loss of coverage.

This tax credit makes affordable, quality health care possible for every South Texan. I’ll keep working with my colleagues in Congress to protect it and ensure families across our district can get the care they need without jeopardizing their financial security.

In South Texas communities like Starr, Hidalgo, and Webb counties, our hospitals and clinics are stretched to the limit. From Rio Grande City to Laredo, doctors and nurses are already working under immense pressure to keep their doors open and families healthy.

After partisan cuts to Medicaid and the looming expiration of health insurance tax credits, the situation is set to become even worse. If Congress fails to act, more than 113,000 people in #TX28 will face higher monthly premiums – making insurance unaffordable altogether for many families.

At @GCHCTexas in Laredo, providers are doing everything they can to avoid cutting staff or reducing services, but the expiration of the tax credits would move the situation from crisis to catastrophe. That means longer ER wait times, fewer staff at clinics, and the real possibility of rural hospitals being forced to scale back or close.

This is unacceptable. I voted against the budget that defunded Medicaid, and I’ll keep fighting to protect it, extend tax credits, and ensure every family in South Texas can access affordable, quality health care.

Here’s the bottom line. The Republican-controlled government is pushing us toward a shutdown because they refuse to negotiate on critical health care tax credits. If Congress doesn’t act, premiums will more than double and families are already getting notices that their costs are set to skyrocket.
 
Without action, a family of four making $125,000 would see their health care costs go up $7,700. A 60-year-old couple making $80,000 would pay $17,500 more. A family of four making $64,000 would pay $2,600 more.
 
Republicans rushed to extend tax cuts for billionaires by July 4. Where is that urgency to help middle-class families, small business owners, veterans, and farmers who are deciding right now if they can afford coverage?
 
I’m fighting to keep the government open, protect your health care, and make sure South Texans don’t get left behind. Watch my full explanation in the video below.

Republican-held districts have the highest Affordable Care Act enrollment, with millions of families depending on subsidies for affordable health care. Farmers, small business owners, and workers without employer coverage are among those who’d be hit hardest if these credits expire.

Yet Republicans are risking a government shutdown by blocking their renewal – a move that’d drive premiums higher and strip coverage from even more Americans, including hundreds of thousands in #TX28.

What’s more, the Republican claim that undocumented immigrants get ACA subsidies is a false narrative they’ve pushed for years. Federal law since 1996 has barred access for undocumented immigrants to federal health benefits. But that didn’t stop Republicans from pushing the same line to sell the American people on the “One Big Beautiful Bill” earlier this year. They’ve recycled this scare tactic for decades, but when premiums rise, Republicans should ask their own constituents if they’re “illegals.”

That’s why I’ll stand firm and keep fighting to protect affordable care.

In Laredo, I hosted a roundtable on the impacts of the government shutdown across South Texas. We covered how the shutdown is affecting local families, federal employees, veterans, farmers, and small businesses, including the potential doubling of health insurance premiums for 113,000 residents in #TX28 if Affordable Care Act tax credits are not extended.

I addressed and corrected false claims about undocumented immigrants receiving federal health benefits, emphasizing the importance of honest and fact-based dialogue. I also shared that I signed a letter refusing my congressional pay. If nearly 15,000 federal employees in TX-28 are going without a paycheck, then neither will I.

The roundtable brought together several community partners and organizations supporting South Texans during this challenging time. I want to thank Mayor Treviño and everyone who joined the discussion for their insights and commitment to our community. 

A government shutdown doesn’t just affect politicians in Washington – it affects real people in our communities. It impacts families, delays paychecks for federal workers, and disrupts services people rely on. I will continue working with colleagues from both parties to find solutions and ensure stability for the people of South Texas.

Today, I joined 143 of my House colleagues in calling on Speaker Johnson to immediately end the Republican-led shutdown and protect Affordable Care Act premium tax credits.

In #TX28, 113,000 residents rely on these credits to afford quality health coverage. Already, some Americans are seeing their costs increase by more than 250%. That’s unacceptable.

With open enrollment just weeks away, we must act now to prevent higher premiums and keep families insured. I’ll continue working in a bipartisan way to reopen the government, lower costs, and protect access to essential care.

ICYMI: The One Big Beautiful Bill, passed in July, already slashed $186 billion from SNAP. With funding set to expire tomorrow, November 1, families are bracing for even greater costs.

Americans are facing higher premiums, rising grocery bills, and growing pressure to cover basic essentials. It doesn’t have to be this way.

We can protect families, strengthen our economy, and ensure access to reliable health care and nutrition – but only if we work together to craft responsible, bipartisan solutions.

Texans battling a life-threatening illness should not have to wait for the care and security they’ve earned.

Too many patients face long delays before they can access Social Security Disability and Medicare benefits.

That’s why I’ve cosponsored the bipartisan Metastatic Breast Cancer Access to Care Act – to eliminate these harmful waiting periods and ensure patients receive vital income and coverage immediately.

This important bill is about compassion, fairness, and being there for patients when it matters most.
